text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.3","verdict":"partly","reason":"The Sentence Combining activity has students expand and combine sentences with appositives and clauses, but the broader language-conventions focus, such as punctuating those structures across writing, is only touched on in the teacher note and not systematically taught."},{"code":"L.6.3.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Sentence Combining activity, students combine Maui sentences with an appositive and a varied opening to vary sentence patterns for meaning and interest."},{"code":"W.6.2","verdict":"partly","reason":"Students draft an introduction and one body paragraph with claim, evidence and analysis, but the full informative essay's selection and organization is not drafted in this lesson and is left to homework."},{"code":"W.6.2.b","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Draft a Body Paragraph activity, students select evidence from a myth and explain it with analysis, developing the topic with concrete details."},{"code":"W.6.2.c","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Draft a Body Paragraph activity, students must use a transition, and the Peer Feedback activity has them check transitions for cohesion."},{"code":"W.6.2.d","verdict":"taught","reason":"Students circle precise academic verbs in the model and must use a precise academic verb in their body paragraph draft."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The Lightning Thief is named in the lesson texts, but the only reference is an invented Percy sentence in the Launch; the evidence students work with is Persephone and Maui, and the model essay is not from the novel."}}
